questions.question: Which instrument is commonly used to measure liquid volume in a laboratory?
Why must a numerical measurement include its unit?
choices: Units guarantee that the value is correct
Units replace the need for an instrument
Units identify the quantity's scale and meaning
Every quantity uses the same unit

questions.question: What is precision in repeated measurements?
choices: How many different units are used
How close a measurement is to the accepted value
How large the measuring instrument is
How closely the measurements agree with each other

questions.question: What is accuracy?
choices: The number of repeated trials alone
How close a measured value is to the accepted value
How similar incorrect measurements are to one another
The number of digits displayed regardless of instrument quality

questions.question: Why should a scale be zeroed before measuring an object's mass?
choices: To avoid including an unwanted offset in the reading

questions.question: How should the bottom of a concave water meniscus usually be read?
choices: At eye level with the liquid surface
At the highest edge while tilting the cylinder

questions.question: Why do measurements have uncertainty?
choices: Units change randomly during a test
Instruments and procedures have limited resolution and other sources of variation

questions.question: Why is a digital display with many digits not sufficient evidence of accuracy?
choices: Extra digits eliminate the need for units
A display can measure only time
An instrument can display many digits while having calibration errors

questions.question: Why should a scientist use an appropriate instrument range?
choices: The instrument must accommodate the quantity and provide useful resolution
Instrument range does not affect usefulness
Any ruler can resolve microscopic structures
The largest instrument is always the most precise
